- Prominent dark/black spherical structure in upper right (characteristic sporangium)
- Substrate appears to be plant stem tissue

**Reference image comparison:**
- **Rhizopus stem (Bugwood_11)**: Showed microscopic sporangiophores with black spherical sporangia — closest structural match to the test image (both show sporangiophore-like stalks + black sporangia)
- **Gray Mold references**: All showed macroscopic brown lesions and ghost spots, not matching the microscopic fungal structure in the test image
- **Sclerotinia stem**: White mycelium with dark sclerotia at soil line — macroscopic, not matching
- **Alternaria stem (Bugwood_13)**: Showed segmented multi-celled conidia — different morphology
- **Powdery Mildew**: White powdery coating on leaf surface — macroscopic, not matching

The black spherical structure in the test image is the key diagnostic feature — it matches Rhizopus sporangia (black, rounded, on stalks). The gray-white filamentous mycelium on plant tissue also fits the Rhizopus description: "whitish-gray mycelia with black sporangia."
